key_insight: SenseWalk simulates human semantic trajectories by combining LLM-driven agent decisions with a social force model to preserve both intent and physical realism.
engineering_relevance: It offers a more accessible workflow for practitioners to generate and analyze movement simulations without requiring deep technical expertise.
method: LLM-powered agents infer semantic goals and behavior from user-defined context.
A social force model enforces realistic motion and interactions in zoned environments.
An interactive interface lets users configure simulations and inspect outputs.
evidence_signal: The paper reports a quantitative experiment for workflow effectiveness and a user study with 12 participants to assess usefulness and efficiency.
watch_item: Simulation quality may depend on prompt design, zone definitions, and the fidelity of the underlying social force assumptions.
paper_title: SenseWalk: Agent-Based Semantic Trajectory Simulation Powered by Large Language Models in Zoned Environments
